The diverse eicosanoid families can be synthesized within brain tumors and may contribute to tumor heterogeneity. This includes cell-specific eicosanoid production involving cancer cells, microglia, infiltrating immune cells, and platelets, each expressing distinct enzymes that facilitate tumor progression and immune evasion. This review examines the various mechanisms underlying brain cancer biology, with a particular focus on the roles of eicosanoids and their signaling pathways and how they affect tumor development, progression, and resistance to therapies. The review also describes therapeutic strategies targeting these pathways. The challenge of reduced responsiveness to therapeutic interventions is addressed through platelet-based drug delivery systems, which can increase efficacy by transporting chemotherapeutic agents directly to cancer cells. These systems also include nanoparticles coated with platelet membranes to evade immune clearance of intact cells and extracellular vesicles that provide high biocompatibility. Finally, tumor-educated platelets-which carry RNA and protein cargo-are presented as noninvasive biomarkers for diagnosing and monitoring disease progression and response to therapies in brain tumors.

title: Immune and inflammatory features associated with pyroptosis- and myocardial fibrosis-related genes in HFpEF: a machine learning study.
abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a heterogeneous syndrome marked by inflammation, immune dysregulation, and myocardial fibrosis. Whether pyroptosis intersects with fibrotic remodeling in HFpEF remains uncertain. Two murine cardiac transcriptomic datasets were integrated after batch correction and intersected with curated pyroptosis- and myocardial fibrosis-related gene sets. Functional enrichment, univariate logistic regression, support vector machine-recursive feature elimination (SVM-RFE), and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression were used for feature selection. Complete separation in the ordinary three-gene logistic fit prompted refitting with Firth bias-reduced logistic regression. Performance was assessed by apparent area under the curve (AUC), stratified bootstrap optimism correction, and repeated nested cross-validation; the panel was re-estimated in a human left-ventricular dataset for exploratory replication. Cell-type Identification by Estimating Relative Subsets of RNA Transcripts (CIBERSORT) estimated immune-cell fractions, and expression was examined in a high-fat diet (HFD)/Nω-nitro-L-arginine methyl ester hydrochloride (L-NAME) murine model and whole blood from patients with HFpEF. Six candidates-Pparg, Ace2, Smad2, Lcn2, Ptpn11, and Sqstm1-were identified. Gene Ontology and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes analyses linked them to SMAD binding, autolysosome/amphisome activity, cellular senescence, efferocytosis, and renin-angiotensin signaling. In the 45-sample discovery cohort, the fixed Pparg-Ptpn11-Ace2 Firth model had an apparent AUC of 1.0000; bootstrap correction yielded an AUC of 0.9971 (95% percentile interval, 0.9780-1.0000). Repeated nested cross-validation produced a mean out-of-fold AUC of 0.9286 (2.5%-97.5% percentile interval, 0.8726-0.9700), revealing additional feature-selection uncertainty. Re-estimation in the human dataset represented panel-level replication rather than validation of a locked cross-species model. No inferred immune-cell fraction differed between HFpEF and control after false-discovery-rate correction, although exploratory correlations were observed among deconvolved fractions and with Ptpn11 expression. HFD/L-NAME-treated mice developed diastolic dysfunction, reduced exercise capacity, pulmonary congestion, cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, and myocardial fibrosis despite preserved systolic function; myocardial Ptpn11, Pparg, and Ace2 transcripts and their proteins were reduced. In patients with HFpEF, whole-blood PTPN11 mRNA was lower than in controls and inversely associated with N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide and C-reactive protein; these unadjusted findings remain exploratory. The three-gene panel is hypothesis-generating rather than a stable diagnostic model; its transportability, selection stability, and clinical relevance require prospective validation.

title: Gingival transcriptomic profiles following initial periodontal therapy reveal differences between Grade B and Grade C periodontitis in B-cell receptor- and Fcγ receptor-related pathways.
abstract: Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease affecting the tooth-supporting tissues. Whether different clinical grades of periodontitis are associated with distinct local gingival molecular profiles remains unclear. This study compared gingival transcriptomic profiles between patients with Grade B and Grade C periodontitis following initial periodontal therapy, with the hypothesis that the two grades would exhibit differences in local immune and biological processes. Gingival tissues were collected after initial periodontal therapy from patients with Grade B or Grade C periodontitis. RNA sequencing was followed by differential gene expression, pathway enrichment, protein-protein interaction, cell-type deconvolution, and transcription factor analyses. Selected genes were validated by qPCR, and key findings were further assessed by immunofluorescence. Among 28,395 genes evaluated, 684 were differentially expressed between Grade C and Grade B periodontitis, including 440 up-regulated and 244 down-regulated genes in Grade C (adjusted p < 0.05, |log₂FC= ≥ 2). Up-regulated genes were enriched in B-cell receptor (BCR) and Fcγ receptor (FcγR) signaling, whereas down-regulated genes were enriched in epithelial differentiation and keratinization pathways. qPCR showed increased transcript levels of the BCR-associated genes CD79A (27-fold, p = 0.0133) and CD79B (3-fold, p = 0.0279) and the FcγR-associated genes FCGR2A (2.6-fold, p = 0.0220) and FCGR3A (3.23-fold, p = 0.0125). These findings suggest that, following initial periodontal therapy, increased expression of immune-related genes and reduced expression of keratinization-related genes are associated with Grade C compared with Grade B periodontitis and warrant further investigation and validation.

title: Inhibition of BMP-Smad1/5 signaling with DMH1 attenuates joint degeneration in a rat model of cuff tear arthropathy.
abstract: To characterize bone morphogenetic protein (BMP) signaling in cuff tear arthropathy (CTA) using a modified rat model (mCTA) and determine whether inhibition of DMH1-sensitive BMP type I receptor signaling attenuates CTA pathology. The rat mCTA model was generated by resection of the supraspinatus and infraspinatus tendons, the superior joint capsule, and the long head of the biceps tendon. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was performed to characterize BMP ligand expression in the humeral head. BMP-2, BMP-7, and phosphorylated Smad1/5 (p-Smad1/5) were evaluated by immunohistochemistry, and Id1 expression was assessed by RT-qPCR. Synovial macrophage subsets were assessed by immunostaining. Rats received daily intraperitoneal DMH1 (10 mg/kg) or vehicle for 4 weeks. Histological scores, bone volume, osteoclast number, inflammatory cytokines, catabolic enzymes, and macrophage markers were quantified. scRNA-seq revealed expression of BMP ligands. In mCTA cartilage, BMP-2 and BMP-7 expression, p-Smad1/5 signaling, and hypertrophic markers (Runx2, Col10a1) were upregulated. DMH1 suppressed Smad1/5 activation, reduced inflammatory and catabolic gene expression, and attenuated cartilage degeneration. In subchondral bone, BMP signaling was associated with increased osteoclast numbers, RANKL/OPG imbalance, and reduced bone volume, all of which were improved by DMH1 treatment. In the synovium, BMP signaling and inflammatory mediators were elevated with increased macrophage numbers; DMH1 reduced inflammatory mediators and M1 macrophage numbers. BMP-Smad1/5 signaling is activated in multiple joint tissues in mCTA and is associated with cartilage degeneration, subchondral bone resorption, and synovial inflammation. These findings suggest that BMP-Smad1/5 signaling may contribute to the pathological changes observed in mCTA.

title: tRNA regulatory ecosystem states shape tissue and circulating small-RNA landscapes in gastric cancer.
abstract: Gastric cancer is a heterogeneous disease shaped by the co-evolution of malignant epithelial programs, stromal remodeling, and immune contexture. Transfer RNA (tRNA) regulation sits at a strategic junction in this biology: it governs translational capacity and selectivity while generating tRNA-derived fragments (tRFs) and tRNA halves (tiRNAs)-a family of regulatory small RNAs detectable in both tissue and blood. We asked whether the coordinated machinery responsible for tRNA transcription, maturation, modification, charging, and cleavage defines biologically meaningful gastric cancer ecosystem states, and whether a corresponding circulating small-RNA phenotype can be detected across independent cohorts of chronic atrophic gastritis (CAG), early gastric cancer (EGC), and gastric cancer (GC). We integrated transcriptomic, genomic, proteomic, and tissue small-RNA data across complementary gastric cancer series and localized the program in single-cell expression maps. The clinical arm comprised independent serum samples from CAG, EGC, and GC participants. A 70-gene tRNA-regulatory program resolved three ecosystem states (TRES-1, TRES-2, and TRES-3). TRES-3 exhibited high tRNA-regulatory activity coupled with proliferative and DNA-repair protein expression, whereas TRES-1 was enriched for receptor-signaling and cell-cycle-restraint proteins. These states also differed in copy-number alterations and non-synonymous variant burden at the program level. Direct tissue small-RNA profiling revealed a marked expansion of tRF output and repertoire breadth in TRES-2 and TRES-3, with state-specific tRF classes, parent-tRNA modules, and exact sequences. A shared set of 446 exact tRF sequences connected the tissue and serum catalogues. In an independent gastric cancer series, the three-state architecture aligned with ACRG molecular subtypes, RNA cargo selection, extracellular vesicle release, and stress-response programs. Single-cell mapping placed tRNA-regulatory activity across epithelial, stromal, and immune compartments. In our serum cohort, the 14-30-nt fraction declined from 47.4% in CAG to 37.8% in EGC and 33.6% in GC, while the 31-40-nt fraction rose from 52.6% to 62.2% and 66.4% (absolute Spearman rho = 0.791; BH-adjusted P = 0.0112; exact-permutation P = 0.0214). tRNA regulation defines gastric cancer ecosystem states with distinct genomic, proteomic, and tissue small-RNA correlates. In our serum cohort, the reciprocal shift in circulating tRF/tiRNA length composition-a decline in the 14-30-nt fraction and a rise in the 31-40-nt fraction-parallels the transition from CAG to EGC to GC. These findings establish a testable molecular framework for paired tissue-serum validation and position circulating tRF/tiRNA architecture as a candidate readout of gastric cancer ecosystem biology.

title: Integrated multi-omics and experimental analyses identify JUNB as a candidate biomarker associated with immune-related processes in psoriasis.
abstract: Psoriasis is an immune-mediated inflammatory skin disease involving abnormal keratinocyte activation and immune infiltration, while the key transcriptional regulators underlying epidermal-immune interactions remain insufficiently defined. To identify and validate core immune-related biomarkers linked to psoriasis pathogenesis, emphasising transcription factor JUNB, through integrated bioinformatics and experimental approaches. Bulk transcriptome datasets (GSE14905, GSE66511, GSE154200) were examined to detect differentially expressed genes (DEGs), while three ML approaches (LASSO, random forest, and XGBoost) were used to identify hub genes. Diagnostic performance was evaluated via ROC curves. Immune infiltration patterns were assessed using CIBERSORT. Single-cell RNA-seq (GSE162183) was used for cellular localization. In vitro experiments were conducted in HaCaT cells stimulated with IL-17A, with JUNB knockdown via siRNA, and expression levels of IL-6, IL-22, and IFNG measured by qRT-PCR. JUNB and S100A7 were consistently upregulated in psoriasis across datasets and showed good diagnostic performance (AUC > 0.85). Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) demonstrated JUNB to be enriched in IL-17, NF-κB, and TNF signalling pathways. Immune analysis indicated JUNB was positively correlated with neutrophils and macrophages. Single-cell analysis confirmed JUNB and S100A7 were primarily expressed in keratinocytes. In vitro, IL-17A stimulation was associated with increased JUNB and S100A7 expression, while JUNB knockdown significantly reduced downstream inflammatory cytokines. These findings indicate that JUNB is closely associated with IL-17-related inflammatory responses and immune infiltration in psoriasis, providing mechanistic context for its involvement in disease pathogenesis and supporting its potential utility as a diagnostic biomarker.

title: Identification of Macrophage Polarization-Related Biomarkers in Multiple Myeloma Using Integrated Bioinformatics.
abstract: Multiple myeloma (MM) is an incurable hematologic neoplasm with heterogeneous prognosis. Within the bone marrow microenvironment, macrophage polarization (MP) contributes to immune remodeling and may influence disease progression, yet MP-related prognostic biomarkers remain insufficiently characterized. In this study, we integrated transcriptomic data from UCSC Xena (n = 844) and GSE4581 (n = 414) to identify differentially expressed genes between immune-hot and immune-cold MM samples stratified by single-sample gene set enrichment analysis (ssGSEA)-derived immune scores. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) and intersection with published MP-related genes yielded candidate genes, which were further refined using univariate Cox regression combined with least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), eXtreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) and support vector machine recursive feature elimination (SVM-RFE) machine learning algorithms to construct a prognostic model. An eight-gene signature (LGALS3, IL2RG, ADAM8, MERTK, ACSS1, ARSK, CBX6 and SOCS3) was established, demonstrating acceptable discriminatory ability for 1-, 2-, and 3-year overall survival (AUC 0.666-0.736 in training cohort). Risk groups differed significantly in immune infiltration patterns, predicted drug sensitivity, and survival outcomes. A predicted competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) network centered on MERTK and SOCS3 was also constructed. These findings identify eight MP-related hub genes as candidate prognostic biomarkers and provide a risk model with acceptable predictive performance, offering insights into the immune-metabolic interplay in MM and suggesting potential avenues for personalized therapeutic strategies.

title: Gene expression signatures from single-cell transcriptomics predict Sjögren's syndrome.
abstract: Sjögren's syndrome (SjS) is a systemic autoimmune disorder characterized by lymphocytic infiltration of exocrine glands, leading to dry eyes and mouth. While previous genome-wide association studies (GWAS) and transcriptomic analyses have identified genes associated with SjS, predictive models based on single-cell resolution are limited. In this study, single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data from peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) of SjS patients were analyzed to map immune cell alterations linked to the disease. Compared with healthy controls, SjS patients displayed decreased proportions of naïve CD8 + T cells and Helios FOXP3 lo CD4 + Tregs, alongside increased frequencies of CTLA-4+ CD8 + inhibitory T cells and TRDC γδ T cells. Using machine learning, a predictive model for SjS diagnosis was developed based on a 12-gene signature (SjS. Sig: GIMAP7, PSMB8, CD27, CCR7, TAGAP, UQCR10, HCLS1, LCK, TNFAIP3, ISG15, GIMAP4, and HLA-DRB1), which effectively differentiated patients from healthy individuals. Key genes such as CD27, PSMB8, HCLS1, LCK, UQCR10, and GIMAP4 were validated in clinical samples through flow cytometry and real-time quantitative PCR. These findings provide insights into the immune landscape of SjS at a single-cell resolution and propose a reliable molecular signature for diagnosis and immune monitoring.

title: Integrated transcriptome and single-cell RNA sequencing identifies transient receptor potential channel-related biomarkers in ulcerative colitis.
abstract: The precise cause of ulcerative colitis (UC) is still unclear. While transient receptor potential (TRP) ion channels are increasingly linked to UC pathophysiology, the comprehensive roles of TRP channel-related genes are not well understood. This study aimed to systematically identify TRP channel-related biomarkers and develop novel diagnostic and therapeutic targets for UC. Transcriptomic data were retrieved from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO). Machine learning algorithms were applied to select signature genes from the overlap between differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and a curated set of 111 transient receptor potential (TRP) channel-related genes. A diagnostic nomogram incorporating signature genes was constructed, and its performance was assessed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration plots, and decision curve analysis (DCA). The cellular landscape was characterized using single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) combined with pseudotime trajectory inference and cell-cell communication analysis. Key results were further validated in a dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced murine colitis model by flow cytometry, multiplex immunohistochemistry, western blotting, and quantitative real-time PCR. Five TRP channel-related feature genes (IL-1β, PIK3R3, ADCY3, ADCY7, and TRPV1) were identified. In UC, IL-1β, PIK3R3, ADCY3, and ADCY7 were notably upregulated, while TRPV1 was markedly downregulated. The nomogram, utilizing these five feature genes, exhibited outstanding discriminatory capability (AUC = 0.993) and provided enhanced net clinical benefit. scRNA-seq analysis identified B and plasma cells as the most significantly expanded pathogenic population, exhibiting acquired bidirectional crosstalk with epithelial cells in UC. Pseudotime trajectory analysis revealed that IL-1β and PIK3R3 were mainly concentrated during the initial developmental phases of B and plasma cells. In the DSS-induced colitis model, there was a notable increase in B-cell infiltration, accompanied by significant upregulation of IL-1β and Pik3r3 at both protein and mRNA levels, with confirmed colocalization with Cd19+ B cells. This study identified five TRP channel-related biomarkers and created a high-performance diagnostic nomogram for UC. The study underscores the pivotal role of B and plasma cells, identifying IL-1β and PIK3R3 as early-activated genes in pathogenic B-cell responses, thus offering new diagnostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets for UC.

title: Prognostic value of APOC1 in patients with acute-on-chronic liver failure.
abstract: Acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) is associated with high short-term mortality. Valid prognostic biomarkers are required to refine risk stratification and improve clinical management. This study aimed to identify potential prognostic biomarkers for predicting clinical outcomes in ACLF patients. Seventy-four ACLF patients admitted to the Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University between January 2021 and April 2022 were enrolled for retrospective analysis of baseline characteristics, clinical parameters and clinical outcomes. Forty patients were randomly selected for data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry (DIA-MS)-based proteomic profiling and differential protein analysis, and categorized into survival (n = 20) and non-survival (n = 20) groups according to 90-day outcomes. Bioinformatics analyses were performed to characterize candidate targets. Apolipoprotein C1 (APOC1) levels were validated by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was used to evaluate its prognostic performance and compare it with a newly established model, conventional biomarkers and existing scoring systems. Single-cell RNA sequencing was applied to determine the cellular source and distribution of APOC1, and molecular docking was performed to screen potential APOC1-targeted therapeutic agents. Proteomic analysis identified 41 differentially expressed proteins (DEPs). Protein-protein interaction network analysis revealed that APOC1 occupied a core hub position in the network. Functional enrichment analysis indicated that DEPs were mainly involved in lipid metabolism, lipoprotein clearance and cholesterol efflux. ELISA confirmed significantly higher plasma APOC1 levels in the survival group, suggesting a protective role. Comparative ROC analysis demonstrated favorable prognostic performance of APOC1. Incorporation of APOC1 into traditional scoring systems moderately improved predictive efficacy. Single-cell RNA sequencing further revealed that APOC1 was predominantly expressed in hepatic macrophages. Molecular docking showed strong binding affinities of APOC1 with saikosaponin D and resveratrol, with binding energies of -7.8 and -6.7 kcal/mol, respectively. Elevated plasma APOC1 was positively correlated with survival in ACLF patients. Plasma APOC1 serves as a novel prognostic biomarker for ACLF. Integrating APOC1 into conventional scoring systems yields complementary prognostic value. Hepatic macrophages represent the primary cellular source of APOC1, and saikosaponin D and resveratrol are promising candidate agents targeting APOC1.

title: Anti-PD-1/CTLA-4 bispecific antibody-based combination therapy for cervical cancer: a multicenter study with biomarker analysis.
abstract: Cadonilimab is a PD-1/CTLA-4 bispecific antibody with robust activity in platinum-pretreated advanced cervical cancer, while its first-line value and resistance mechanisms remain unclear. This multicenter retrospective study enrolled 52 treatment-naive patients with recurrent/metastatic cervical cancer (R/M CC) receiving cadonilimab plus chemotherapy. We assessed clinical efficacy and safety, and performed RNA-seq and immunohistochemistry for exploratory biomarker analysis. The 2-year overall survival, 2-year progression-free survival and objective response rate were 82.6%, 66.7% and 75.0%, respectively. Main treatment-related adverse events included myelosuppression, thyroid dysfunction, gastrointestinal reactions and fatigue, demonstrating acceptable safety. Transcriptomic data showed suppressed Hippo, NF-κB, RIG-1 pathways and reduced M1-macrophage polarization in patients with longer PFS. Candidate genes including GGT6 and FRG2 were identified as putative resistance-associated markers in this small exploratory cohort. Higher M1-macrophage polarization and p-STAT1 expression were observed in short-PFS patients, indicating a possible link between p-STAT1 activation and M1-macrophage enrichment. Of note, outcomes should be interpreted considering the retrospective single-arm design and limited sample size. Cadonilimab-containing regimen achieved promising efficacy and an acceptable safety profile as first-line therapy for R/M CC. The biomarker findings are exploratory and provide preliminary evidence for future research on bispecific-antibody resistance.

title: GeoMx Digital Spatial Profiler Enables Layer-Specific Spatial Transcriptomic Profiling of the Human Retina: A Proof-of-Concept Study from Post-Coronovirus Disease 2019 Donor Tissue.
abstract: To generate layer resolved spatial transcriptomic profiles of the human retina using NanoString GeoMx Digital Spatial Profiler (DSP) and evaluate whether this approach can be successfully applied to resolve spatially localized transcriptional changes across retinal compartments in diseased retina. Study of human postmortem retinal tissue using spatial transcriptomics with cross-platform computational validation. Postmortem human retinal samples from donors with and without history of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19). Anatomically defined retinal layers were profiled using GeoMx DSP with layer-resolved region of interest selection. Data were validated using retinal layer markers, and concordance with published single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) reference signatures was established. Differential expression and pathway-level comparisons were performed between donors with and without a history of COVID-19, with emphasis on spatial localization of changes across retinal layers. (1) Concordance of GeoMx layer resolved expression with known photoreceptor and retinal pigment epithelium marker patterns and scRNA-seq reference signatures; (2) exploratory identification of candidate layer restricted gene expression differences in donors with a history of COVID-19, as a proof-of-concept application of the platform. GeoMx DSP captured biologically expected, layer-specific transcriptional changes across the human retina, including compartmentalized layer expression, and showed cross-platform concordance with published scRNA-seq reference signatures. In an exploratory comparison of donors with and without a history of COVID-19, candidate gene expression differences were observed across specific retinal layers, suggesting spatially nonuniform transcriptional patterns that warrant further investigation in larger independently validated cohorts. Layer-resolved GeoMx DSP provides a robust approach for spatial transcriptomic analysis of human retina and enables scRNA informed interpretation through cross platform benchmarking. Exploratory application to donors with COVID-19 history identified spatially restricted transcriptional shifts across retinal compartments, illustrating the utility of layer resolved retinal spatial transcriptomics as a discovery framework for studying clinically relevant perturbations and informing future ocular disease and therapeutic research.
